span.label: The sufficient condition proved is not sharp; the numerical experiments only show it is within a constant factor of the achievable bound.
span.note: what this limits: the sharpness of the sufficient condition: OUR METHODS DO NOT QUITE ATTAIN THIS THEORETICAL UPPER BOUND FOR CORRECT RECOVERY, [and] OUR NUMERICAL EXPERIMENTS SUGGEST THAT THEY DO COME WITHIN A CONSTANT FACTOR - the gap is measured, not proved
span.quote: While our methods do not quite attain this theoretical upper bound for correct recovery, our numerical experiements suggest that they do come within a constant factor of this bound (see Figure 2).

span.label: The particular dual polynomial construction used in the proof is a known source of looseness.

span.quote: One source of slack in the theoretical analysis is the way in which we choose the polynomial P (t) (as in (2.11)).

span.label: Robustness to measurement error is not established; under perturbation exact recovery no longer holds and only preliminary calculations are offered.
span.note: what this limits: the noiseless case only: under measurement perturbation, ONE CANNOT EXPECT EXACT RECOVERY
span.quote: In this setup, of course, one cannot expect exact recovery.

span.label: The deterministic uniqueness theorem depends on the signal length being prime.

span.quote: Note that if N is not prime, the lemma (and hence the theorem) fails, essentially because of the presence of non-trivial subgroups of ZN with addition modulo N ; see [6], [18] for further discussion.

span.label: The robust uncertainty principle underlying the analysis is stated but not developed here.
